name: Arakkal Kettu (Arakkal Museum)
tagline: The palace‑museum of Kerala’s only Muslim royal family, on Kannur’s coast
summary: Durbar hall of the Arakkal royal family in Ayikkara, converted into a small museum of maritime and royal artefacts; a key stop on coastal heritage walks around Kannur.
description: Arakkal Kettu is the former palace (durbar hall) of the Arakkal Ali Rajas, the only Muslim royal family of Kerala; a part of the complex in Ayikkara is now the Arakkal Museum. It sits close to Mappila Bay and St. Angelo Fort and combines Kerala and colonial architectural features.

The museum displays family heirlooms and maritime material culture — the family seal, pathayam (wooden grain chest), royal copies of the Quran, swords and daggers, an old telephone and a telescope — tracing the Arakkal dynasty’s trade and sea connections.

Arakkal Kettu matters for coastal history and plural heritage in Kannur: the site links local maritime trade, colonial encounters and the matrilineal Arakkal household. It is increasingly featured in local heritage walks and conservation plans for the Ayikkara heritage street.
Visitors get a compact, close‑up sense of Kannur’s coastal past and the Arakkal family’s role; the museum pairs well with a walk around Mappila Bay and a visit to St. Angelo Fort.
highlights: Durbar hall turned family museum with maritime artefacts
Objects: family seal, pathayam, royal Qur’ans, weapons, telescope
Located in Ayikkara near Mappila Bay and St. Angelo Fort
Part of a designated Heritage Zone under Kannur master plan
Included in recent Kannur heritage walks and trail programmes

sections.heading: Background
body: Arakkal Kettu is the palace complex of the Arakkal dynasty, a matrilineal ruling family that held authority around Kannur and over nearby islands. Historians place the family’s prominence from the late medieval period; the palace shows a blend of traditional Kerala and colonial architecture.

A portion of the palace (the durbar/administrative block) is conserved as the Arakkal Museum and managed by the Arakkal family trust in partnership with state archaeology/cultural bodies. The site forms the core of the Ayikkara heritage street protected under Kannur’s Master Plan.

sections.heading: What to see and do
body: Browse the compact galleries in the durbar hall: family documents and household furniture, the wooden pathayam chest, royal Qur’ans and small maritime‑related objects that illustrate trade links with European powers and local seafaring life.

Use the museum as the start or midpoint of a short coastal heritage walk — Mappila Bay, St. Angelo Fort and the Ayikkara shoreline sit within easy walking distance and together tell the story of Kannur’s harbour, colonial encounters and local communities.
Photography and detailed documentation norms vary; be respectful in the small gallery spaces and around adjacent mosque and residential areas.

sections.heading: Plan your visit
body: Location and hours recorded on official tourism listings: the museum is on Ayikkara Government Hospital Road, near the District Hospital in Ayikkara. Published visiting hours are usually 10:00–17:00 and the museum is closed on Mondays (confirm before you travel).

Nearest rail: Kannur railway station (about 3 km). Nearest airport: Kannur International Airport (roughly 25–26 km). Combine the museum with St. Angelo Fort and the Ayikkara shoreline for a half‑day heritage loop.

latest.text: City Heritage’s 'Veru' programme (May 2–3, 2026) documented and ran a Kannur Heritage Trail that traced Mappila Bay and the legacies of the Arakkal Kingdom, boosting local heritage‑walk visibility.
Kannur City Master Plan (2041) formally marks Arakkal Kettu / Arakkal Museum and the surrounding Ayikkara street as a Heritage Zone with protection and facade/height controls.

visitorInfo.howToReach: Ayikkara (near District Hospital) in Kannur city; Kannur railway station ≈3 km, Kannur International Airport ≈25–26 km. Walks from St. Angelo Fort and Mappila Bay make easy heritage circuits.
etiquette: Check opening hours and the nominal entry fee before you go (official listings record 10:00–17:00 and a small fee; closed Mondays).
Dress modestly and be respectful around nearby mosque and residential areas.
Pair with St. Angelo Fort and a walk around Mappila Bay for a full coastal‑history experience.
Confirm guided‑walk schedules or heritage‑trail events in advance if you want an interpretive walk.
